headline: Indian students protest after a medical exam leak

sources.title: India opposition leader Gandhi freed after detention at student-led protest
Thousands protest in India after clashes, despite Modi assuring action on exams

chunks.text: More than 5,000 people [[gathered]] at Jantar Mantar, a protest site in Delhi, on Tuesday, July 22, [[a day after]] clashes {{broke out}} between police and marchers. The protest is over a national medical entrance exam whose papers leaked in May, forcing about two million candidates to take the test again. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Vadra were [[detained]] outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence and released that evening.

chunks.text: The protests are organized by the Cockroach Janta Party, which {{grew out of}} an online joke two months ago and has since [[gained]] millions of followers. Led mainly by students, it wants Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to {{step down}}, the release of Sonam Wangchuk, an activist on hunger strike since June 28, and 10 million rupees, about $104,000, for each family of the dozen or so students who died.

chunks.text: Monday's march toward parliament ended in violence, with police using tear gas and batons to {{hold back}} the [[crowd]]. Delhi Police said nearly 180 people were hurt, including 118 police and security staff and 60 protesters. The party's [[founder]], Abhijeet Dipke, said more than 150 protesters were in hospitals. Neither figure has been [[independently]] checked. Modi told lawmakers that his government acted [[as soon as]] it {{found out}} about the leak, that 13 people had been arrested, and that the re-test {{went ahead}} without problems.

chunks.text: Pradhan said students [[deserve]] [[far better than]] being treated as props in a political [[campaign]]. Hundreds {{stayed on}} at Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, and smaller protests were held in Mumbai and Bengaluru. The re-test is finished, but the party says it will {{keep up}} its protests until the government {{brings in}} changes to the way exams are run.
